To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have measured and correlated the densities and visco- sities of the pure fatty acid ethyl and methyl minor esters present in biodiesel fuel.

the density and viscosity of the pure fatty acid methyl and ethyl esters of interest can be predicted with an average absolute error of less than 2 % and 10 %, respectively, using a predictive model that uses group contribution methods and temperature-dependent coefficients.
we have developed a method to predict densities of fatty esters, and that the method is accurate within 1.2 %.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determination of physical properties (densities and viscosities) of pure fatty acid ethyl and methyl minor components of biodiesels.
the development of models to predict the behavior of biodiesels.
the study of the thermophysical properties of biodiesel components.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the group contribution methods are able to predict the density of pure biodiesel components, but not the viscosity.
the predictive methods of Ceriani et al., GCVOL, and the UNIFAC model can predict the density of pure ethyl and pure methyl esters within 1.0, 1.5, and 1.5 %, respectively.
the GCVOL model is the most suitable for density predictions and that the method of Ceriani is the most suitable to predict viscosities of these compounds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GCVOL model is able to predict densities of the pure esters with an average absolute deviation (AARD) of 0.9 %.
we were able to measure the densities and visosities of the minor components of biodiesels and propose correlations for the densities and viscosity with temperature.
the GCVOL method is able to predict the densities of pure methyl and ethyl esters of fatty acids within 1.2 % and viscosities within 3 %.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we were able to measure the densities and visosities of pure ethyl and pure methyl esters of biodiesel minor components, and we were able to predict them with a good level of confidence using the GCVOL method for densities and the method of Ceriani and co-workers for viscosities.
the densities and viscoities of these compounds can be predicted with good accuracy using existing models.
it is possible to predict the densities of biodiesels with an error of less than 1.5% and viscosities within 2.2%.
